_about: Dated changes of the rules that touch daily life in London, 1931-1940, for the engine. 'sure': confirmed by the source given; 'check': the date or figure is from secondary sources or not fully confirmed. Prices in pence.

changes.what: Labour Government resigns; National Government under Ramsay MacDonald
Britain leaves the gold standard
Unemployment benefit cut by a tenth: a single man 17s. to 15s. 3d.; a married man with wife from 30s. to 27s. 3d.
changes.status: check: rates sure (Hansard 23 Mar 1932), effective date not confirmed

changes.what: General election: National Government returned with a great majority
The means test: after 26 weeks, 'transitional payments' only after a household means test by the Public Assistance Committee
changes.status: check: month sure, day not confirmed

changes.what: London Passenger Transport Board takes over the trams, buses and Underground
Unemployment benefit cuts fully restored (Unemployment Act 1934): a single man 17s. again
Silver Jubilee of King George V: a public holiday, streets decorated
Stanley Baldwin Prime Minister
General election
Death of King George V; Edward VIII King
Battle of Cable Street in the East End
The Crystal Palace burns down; the glow is seen across London
Abdication of Edward VIII; George VI King
Coronation of George VI: a public holiday
Neville Chamberlain Prime Minister
Munich crisis: gas masks issued to Londoners, trenches dug in the parks
Munich Agreement: 'peace for our time'
Evacuation of schoolchildren from London begins; the blackout
Britain declares war on Germany; men 18-41 liable to call-up (National Service (Armed Forces) Act)
Petrol rationing
National Register taken; identity cards
Food rationing: bacon and ham 4 oz, butter 4 oz, sugar 12 oz a person a week
changes.status: sure for the date; amounts as usually given

changes.what: Meat rationed by price
changes.status: check: day and the value per person differ between sources

changes.what: Winston Churchill Prime Minister
Dunkirk evacuation (to 4 June)
Tea (2 oz), margarine and cooking fats rationed
changes.status: check: month sure, day not confirmed

changes.what: The Blitz begins: 'Black Saturday', the Surrey Commercial Docks in Rotherhithe and Bermondsey set on fire; raids on London nearly every night after

steady._about: Rules that did not change in the decade (as far as checked)
steady.old_age_pension: 10s. a week at 70 (non-contributory, means-tested), and at 65 for the insured (contributory)
steady.licensing_london: weekdays 11.30-3 and 5.30-11; Sundays 12.30-2.30 and 7-10 (Licensing Act 1921; not checked against a source)
